lines: A sixteen channel step sequencer of sixteen pads per channel, with an Open Sound Control interface for driving it from a tablet or another program
Sets the tempo of the internal clock, from a quarter of the note value per minute up to sixty-four times it, and the reading above shows the result
Starts and stops playback, and the lamp on it shows whether the sequence is running
Sends playback back to the first step, and while playback is stopped arms step one for the next start
Sets how many steps the sequence plays before it returns to the first, 1 to 16
Picks which of the 64 patterns is played, which is the number under PATT on the left of the display
Picks which of the 64 patterns the pads and knobs are editing, which is the number under PATT on the right of the display
Picks which of the sixteen channels the pads and knobs are editing, 1 to 16, shown under CHNL and coloured to match that channel's output jack
Picks the output mode of the channel being edited: TRIG gives a short pulse on each active step, RTRG gives a pulse everywhere except the active steps, and GATE holds 10V for the whole step
Copies the whole pattern being edited, all sixteen channels, to the clipboard
Copies the channel being edited, in the pattern being edited, to the clipboard
Pastes whatever was last copied into the pattern or channel being edited
Steps the clock division through 1/4, 1/8, 1/8T and 1/16, which changes what the tempo knob counts and is shown after BPM on the display
Turns the OSC connection on and saves the addresses and ports typed into the configuration screen
Switched on, the OSC connection is opened again whenever the patch is loaded
Shows and hides the OSC configuration screen, where the send and receive addresses and ports are typed
A rising edge here sets the tempo of the internal clock, -10V for the slowest setting and 10V for the fastest
A rising edge here advances the sequence one step and takes over from the internal clock while a cable is present
A rising edge here sends playback back to the first step
Sets how many steps the sequence plays, -10V for one step and 10V for 16
Picks which pattern is played, -10V for pattern 1 and 10V for pattern 64
Switches that step of the channel being edited on or off
Carries that channel's output, and the ring of light around the jack shows when that channel is firing
Note — the pads and knobs edit one channel of one pattern at a time, chosen by the CHNL knob and the PATT knob under EDIT; the PATT knob under PLAYBACK is the one that plays
Note — each of the sixteen channels keeps its own output mode, so the MODE knob changes the mode of the channel being edited rather than of the whole module
Note — dragging across the pads with the mouse held down toggles every pad the pointer passes over, which is the quickest way to draw or clear a run of steps
Note — hovering a step and pressing the copy key copies that step, and the paste key pastes a step, row or column back; the same actions are on the step's own right-click menu
Note — with nothing patched to the clock jack the module runs from its own clock at the tempo set by the tempo knob; patching a clock there takes that over
Note — an output goes to 10V when its step is on and 0V when it is off, and in TRIG mode the 10V lasts only for the clock pulse
Menu — Initialize (Reset Channel Mode) — a heading over three items that clear steps and put the output mode back to its default
Menu — Current Edit Channel — clears the channel being edited in the pattern being edited
Menu — Current Edit Pattern — clears all sixteen channels of the pattern being edited
Menu — All Patterns — clears every channel of all 64 patterns
Menu — Initialize (Keep Channel Mode) — a heading over the same three items, which clear the steps but leave each channel's output mode alone
Menu — Random Options — a heading over the two randomisers below it
Menu — > All Steps Random — gives every step of the channel being edited a fresh random value
Menu — > Structured Random — randomises the channel being edited in a pattern rather than step by step
Menu — Set Value — on a step's own right-click menu, picks that step's value from a list instead of by dragging
Menu — Copy Step — on a step's own right-click menu, copies that step to the clipboard
Menu — Copy Row — on a step's own right-click menu, copies the whole row that step is in
Menu — Copy Column — on a step's own right-click menu, copies the whole column that step is in
Menu — Paste Step — on a step's own right-click menu, pastes a copied step here
Menu — Paste Row — on a step's own right-click menu, pastes a copied row starting here
Menu — Paste Column — on a step's own right-click menu, pastes a copied column starting here
Menu — Clear Clipboard — on a step's own right-click menu, throws away whatever was copied

lines: A sixteen channel step sequencer of sixty-four steps per channel, where each channel can put out triggers, gates or voltages, with an Open Sound Control interface
Sets the tempo of the internal clock, from a quarter of the note value per minute up to sixty-four times it, and the reading above shows the result
Starts and stops playback, and the lamp on it shows whether the sequence is running
Sends playback back to the first step, and while playback is stopped arms step one for the next start
Sets how many steps the sequence plays before it returns to the first, 1 to 64
Picks which of the 64 patterns is played, which is the number under PATT on the left of the display
Picks which of the 64 patterns the pads and knobs are editing, which is the number under PATT on the right of the display
Picks which of the sixteen channels the pads and knobs are editing, 1 to 16, shown under CHNL and coloured to match that channel's output jack
Picks the output mode of the channel being edited, from TRIG, RTRG and GATE for pulses and gates through VOLT, NOTE and PATT for voltages
Copies the whole pattern being edited, all sixteen channels, to the clipboard
Copies the channel being edited, in the pattern being edited, to the clipboard
Pastes whatever was last copied into the pattern or channel being edited
Steps the clock division through 1/4, 1/8, 1/8T and 1/16, which changes what the tempo knob counts and is shown after BPM on the display
Turns the OSC connection on and saves the addresses and ports typed into the configuration screen
Switched on, the OSC connection is opened again whenever the patch is loaded
Shows and hides the OSC configuration screen, where the send and receive addresses and ports are typed
A rising edge here sets the tempo of the internal clock, -10V for the slowest setting and 10V for the fastest
A rising edge here advances the sequence one step and takes over from the internal clock while a cable is present
A rising edge here sends playback back to the first step
Sets how many steps the sequence plays, -10V for one step and 10V for 64
Picks which pattern is played, -10V for pattern 1 and 10V for pattern 64
Sets what that step of the channel being edited puts out; in the trigger modes it toggles the step on and off, and in the voltage modes it sets a value
Carries that channel's output, and the ring of light around the jack shows when that channel is firing

Menu — Set Value — on a step's own right-click menu, picks that step's value from a list instead of by dragging
Menu — Copy Step — on a step's own right-click menu, copies that step to the clipboard
Menu — Copy Row — on a step's own right-click menu, copies the whole row that step is in
Menu — Copy Column — on a step's own right-click menu, copies the whole column that step is in
Menu — Paste Step — on a step's own right-click menu, pastes a copied step here
Menu — Paste Row — on a step's own right-click menu, pastes a copied row starting here
Menu — Paste Column — on a step's own right-click menu, pastes a copied column starting here
Menu — Clear Clipboard — on a step's own right-click menu, throws away whatever was copied
Menu — Song Mode — clears the list of patterns the song plays, and appears only while song mode is available
Menu — Shift Values — a heading over the two items below it
Menu — > +1 V/Octave/Patt — raises every step by one volt, one octave or one pattern, over a submenu of Current Edit Channel, Current Edit Pattern or All Patterns
Menu — > -1 V/Octave/Patt — lowers every step by one volt, one octave or one pattern, over the same three choices
Shows and hides the song mode screen, where the list of patterns the song plays is set
